newsitem.title: USA: NBC unveils fall TV programs.
newsitem.headline: NBC unveils fall TV programs.

text.p: General Electric Co's National Broadcasting Co formally unveiled its fall prime time televison lineup on Monday, a schedule blanketed by comedy programs.

The network, which is assured of at least one more season of Jerry Seinfeld in the Thursday night show by that name, said it will fill the 8 pm through 10 pm blocs from Monday to Thursday nights with comedies, including five new half-hour sitcoms. The network said it will also add a new weekend sitcom "Jenny" and two dramas, including "Sleepwalkers" a sci-fi thriller which will air Saturdays at 9 pm.

Among the most closely-watched of the new shows are expected to be "Veronica's Closet", which will air Thursday night at 9:30, before "ER." A half-hour sitcom about the owner of a women's lingerie company, it will have a cast led by Kirstie Alley, who was a regular on the long-running hit "Cheers." Its executive producers are the creators of another NBC hit, "Friends."

Another newcomer is "The Tony Danza Show", which will lead the lineup on Wednesday nights at 8 pm. That show stars Danza, from "Who's The Boss" as a divorced sportswriter raising two teenage daughers.

NBC will unveil another new program, "Built To Last." on Wednesday nights at 8:30. It stars standup comic Royale Watkins and veteran actor Paul Winfield, who plays the owner of a black family's construction business.

NBC is capitalizing on the popularity of Jenny McCarthy, the host of MTV's dating game show "Singled Out" by giving her a show, which airs Sunday evenings at 8:30. Mccarthy and costar Heather Paige Kent play best friends who move from Utica, N.Y. to seek their fame in Hollywood.
The network will use a one-hour slot on Friday night at 8 pm to air a new show, "Players", starring Ice-T as one of three former convicts who go to work for the federal government.
"Suddenly Susan", starring Brooke Shields, is moving to Monday at 8 pm.
